record.paper_title: Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures: current trends and open problems
record.original_question: Develop big Ramsey degree theory for uncountable homogeneous structures, including the Ramsey theorems on trees of uncountable height needed to support such characterizations. Existing work characterizes examples such as the kappa-rationals and kappa-Rado graph under large-cardinal consistency assumptions, but the broader field for uncountable homogeneous structures remains open.

evidence.quote: The field of big Ramsey degrees for uncountable homogeneous structures is still quite open, but the fleshing out of the Ramsey theorems on trees of uncountable height has seen some recent work in [19], [20], and [68].
Džamonja, Larson, and Mitchell applied a slight modification of his theorem to characterize the big Ramsey degrees for the κ-rationals and the κ-Rado graph.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A homogeneous structure is a countable or uncountable relational structure M such that every isomorphism between finitely generated substructures of M extends to an automorphism of M. For an infinite structure M and a finite substructure A ⊆ M, the big Ramsey degree T(A,M) is the least integer T (if it exists) such that for every finite coloring of the copies of A in M, there is a substructure M' ⊆ M isomorphic to M in which the copies of A take at most T colors.

Now let κ be an uncountable cardinal (assume any necessary large-cardinal hypotheses, e.g. κ measurable, so that the Halpern–Läuchli theorem holds for the tree 2^{<κ}). Examples of uncountable homogeneous structures of size κ include:
 (i) the κ-rationals: the unique κ-saturated dense linear order without endpoints of cardinality κ;
 (ii) the κ-Rado graph: the unique κ-saturated homogeneous-universal graph of cardinality κ;
together with κ-versions of further Fraïssé-type limits and universal inverse-limit structures.

Problem. Develop a general theory of big Ramsey degrees for uncountable homogeneous structures. Specifically:
 (a) Formulate and prove the Ramsey theorems for colorings of finite antichains, embedded subtrees, and strong subtrees of trees of uncountable height (e.g. 2^{<κ} and more general κ-branching trees) that are needed to support such a theory.
 (b) Using these tree-Ramsey theorems, characterize for each finite substructure A of a given uncountable homogeneous structure M of size κ whether T(A,M) is finite, and if so compute its exact value, for broad classes of uncountable homogeneous structures beyond the κ-rationals and κ-Rado graph (e.g. κ-versions of the triangle-free graph, generic partial order, ultrametric spaces, and other κ-Fraïssé limits).

artifact.status_search_result: The field of big Ramsey degrees for uncountable homogeneous structures is widely described as still largely open. Existing results (Shelah's Halpern–Läuchli theorem at measurable κ, and the Džamonja–Larson–Mitchell characterizations for the κ-rationals and κ-Rado graph) cover only a few cases under large-cardinal assumptions, and recent surveys list general big Ramsey degree theory for uncountable homogeneous structures and the corresponding Ramsey theorems on trees of uncountable height as an open research program.
